top_needs.title: Practice efficiency gains and ROI with DM-monitored braces and aligners versus standard recall
top_needs.brands_and_products: Damon, ormco, Spark, Invisalign, suresmile, clearcorrect, KLOwen, Lightforce, self-ligating braces, Twin brackets, SmartSTL, ScanBox
top_needs.metrics_sought: chair time reduction, appointment frequency, ROI, profitability, time saving, visit reduction, rentability, ongoing monitoring costs vs benefits, adaptive aligner change, efficiency in second and third order movements, average visit reduction, decrease of emergencies
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors question whether DM actually saves time or money, reduces appointments, or improves practice profitability. Some are skeptical that the workflow changes will translate into real efficiency or financial gains, especially for braces cases.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, case study, white paper, No format preference specified — reps asked for any available evidence
sample_queries: How much chair time reduction achieved
Show how can doctors increases the profitability if their practices using DM
Could you provide any data demonstrating improved patient compliance with DM or its impact on patient outcomes
How can I make DM work in a practice with 8 chairs and 15 assistants in a way that they really get the real benefits and make it work financially as well in The Netherlands?
Are Damon brackets more efficient than other brands?
top_needs.gap_assessment: Direct comparative studies quantifying ROI and efficiency for DM-monitored braces versus aligners and standard care are limited. More robust, region-specific economic analyses and workflow impact studies are needed.

top_needs.title: Accuracy and reliability of DM’s AI and SmartSTL for clinical monitoring and diagnostics
top_needs.metrics_sought: AI accuracy, specificity and sensitivity, reliability, accuracy of SmartSTL, accuracy class I goal, occlusal assessment, FDA application, accuracy of scanning, AI versus orthodontist
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors are skeptical about whether DM’s AI can reliably detect clinical changes, match or exceed human accuracy, or be trusted for diagnostics. Some express distrust or fear of AI replacing clinical judgment.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, clinical study, white paper, No format preference specified — reps asked for any available evidence
sample_queries: Information on the accuracy of DM, a patient has questioned the ability of the AI to detect clinical observations

Occlusal Assessment: A quantitative study validating the AI’s accuracy in detecting malocclusions (midline deviation, overbite, overjet, and canine relationship) found that the mean bias across all parameters was less than 0.5 mm, confirming its reliability as a remote diagnosis and triage tool.
How accurate is DentalMonitorings AI and will it save me money
Looking for white papers on Smart STL accuracy to help convince a doctor to use it in the practice.
Is Smart STL like an intraoralscan?
top_needs.gap_assessment: Peer-reviewed, head-to-head accuracy studies (AI vs. orthodontist, SmartSTL vs. intraoral scan) are sparse. More validation studies and regulatory-grade evidence are needed to address skepticism.
